lines.text: Why is it so cold in winter?
Why is the grass white in the morning?

lines: Great questions! Let's find out how the weather works.
Remember, the Earth is a little bit tilted.
In summer, your side leans toward the Sun. The Sun climbs high in the sky, and the days are long.
In winter, the Sun stays low, and the days are short.
Look at these two flashlights.
When light shines straight down, it makes a small, strong spot. That's like summer sunshine. It warms the ground a lot.
When light comes in at a slant, it spreads out and gets weaker. That's like winter sunshine. So it's colder!
Every day, the Sun warms the ground.
At night there is no Sun, so the ground lets its warmth float away, up into the sky.
On a clear night, the warmth escapes easily, and it gets really cold.
Clouds work like a blanket. They keep some of the warmth in.
That's why the coldest time is often early in the morning, just before the Sun comes up.
Now, water.
When the Sun warms a puddle, a lake, or the sea, some water turns into an invisible gas called water vapor.
It floats in the air all around us. How much water vapor is in the air is called humidity.
Warm air can hold lots of water vapor. Cold air can hold less.
Have you seen a cold glass of water get wet on the outside?
The cold glass cools the air around it, and the water vapor turns back into tiny drops.
The same thing happens on the grass at night. When the grass gets cold, little drops appear. That's dew.
But on a winter night, the grass can get colder than freezing.
Then the water vapor turns straight into tiny ice crystals. That's frost!
When the Sun comes up and warms the grass, the frost melts away.
So where does rain come from?
The Sun warms the sea, and water vapor rises up with the warm air.
High in the sky it is cold, so the vapor turns into tiny droplets. Lots and lots of them make a cloud!
The droplets bump together and grow bigger and heavier.
When they get too heavy, they fall down as rain.
The rain flows into rivers and back to the sea, and it all starts again. This is called the water cycle.
When it's very cold up in the cloud, the water turns into ice crystals instead.
They grow into beautiful snowflakes. Every snowflake has six arms!
If the air stays cold all the way down, they land as snow.
If the air near the ground is warm, the snowflakes melt and land as rain. In fact, a lot of rain starts as snow, high up in the sky!
So: the tilt of the Earth gives us seasons.
The Sun warms the day, and clear nights get cold.
Cold grass gives us dew and frost.
And warm, wet air rising up gives us clouds, rain, and snow!
